web_evidence.title: Auntie Mame An Irreverent Escapade
web_evidence.note: The licensed Chapter One excerpt supplied with the Crown edition opens with the participating narrator discussing his own day as I and my, then recounts his childhood as I; it establishes first-person narration in the opening and ensuing flashback.

web_evidence.title: Laughing the Cold War Away with Auntie Mame
web_evidence.note: Alessandro Clericuzio's scholarly structural analysis states that the story is told from Patrick's point of view and identifies Patrick as the narrator; its quotations from the novel repeatedly show his participating I, we, and my narration.

web_evidence.title: MAME Teacher's Instructional Guide: From Page to Stage
web_evidence.note: The educational guide reproduces original-book pages 16–17, where Patrick narrates Mame's actions toward me and concludes that I knew I was safe, corroborating first-person narration early in the novel.

person_note: The controlling narrator is Patrick, who participates in the events and retrospectively recounts his life with Auntie Mame in the first person. Quote q00895 independently exposes this base voice through the narratorial clause I immediately wrote down, while the authorized opening excerpt and Tier B scholarly analysis agree. Third-person descriptions of Mame, Mother Burnside, and other subjects are descriptions made by Patrick, not evidence of a separate third-person narrator; first-person dialogue spoken by Mame is local speech. No credible research found sustained narration in another person. The principal coverage limitation is that the Tier A prose is from the opening, but the whole-book scholarly account resolves that limitation and supports high confidence.
